---
title: "The command line"
---

Today we will work with the very basics of bioinformatics - the command line. We will get to know what it is and why it is so popular. You will learn how to move around directories, create, read and edit files. 

This will be the basis for other modules in the course. On the course server you will use the same commands.

## Learning outcomes

After today you can:

- explain what a shell is and why we use it for bioinformatics
- tell absolute and relative paths apart, and write both
- move around folders with `pwd`, `ls` and `cd`
- create, copy, move and delete files and folders with `mkdir`, `touch`, `cp`, `mv` and `rm`
- create and edit a text file with `nano`
- read a file with `cat`, `less` and `head`, and use wildcards like `*`
